docs.title: Welcome to the Incar Skill System
docs.text:
This documentation contains general information regarding the installation and usage. The incar skill system consists of three main components:

  • The core system, which handles most of the logic, networking, data collection, training, and running of models.
  • A teleoperation app for the Meta Quest 3, which allows you to stream trajectories and other inputs.
  • A robot implementation that interprets the commands. Since each robot is different, you might need to build this component yourself, however we do provide building blocks for easy integration. Furthermore, implementations for the Viper 300S, ufactory lite6, and Franka Panda robots are available.

Info

The Incar Teleop app is not yet publicly available, contact us for help with installation.

docs.title: Getting Started.
docs.text:
To install the core system, run:

mkdir incar_ws && cd incar_ws
python -m venv venv_incar
source bin/activate
git clone https://github.com/INCAR-Robotics/core.git
cd core
pip install -e .

Info

If you get an error that the directory can not be installed in editable mode, try first running pip install --upgrade pip

To start up the core system, run

python core/incar/manager.py

Use the GUI to connect your teleoperation app and robot, and to teleoperate the robots, play skills, or collect datasets.

docs.title: Dataset Structure.
docs.text:
A dataset has the following structure:

example_ds/
├── demo_0/
│   ├── example_feature/
│   │   └── data.h5
│   ├── video_feature/
│   │   ├── data.mp4
│   │   └── timestamps.h5
│   └── meta.json
├── demo_1/
│   └── ...
├── demo_2/
│   └── ...
└── dataset_config.json

A demo is one recording consisting of various features. Features can be an of one of the following types:

  • "VISUAL": these are image types
  • "STATE": these are arrays of floats that can be read from the robot system (e.g. joint states, force sensors)
  • "ACTION": these are arrays of floats that are input into the robot system (e.g. a cartesian velocity command)
  • "TEXT": this can be used for serializing any other data, e.g. user input button data can be saved as a json string.

Each dataset has a config file named dataset_config.json which describes the features and their shapes that are present in the dataset. Furthermore each demo has a meta.json file which describes when the demo was recorded, statistics used for normalization as well as some other information.

docs.title: Creating a dataset
docs.text:
You can create a dataset by manually creating a folder with a dataset_config.json, or directly from the GUI. An example of the dataset_config.json file can be found below:

{
    "version": "0.0.1",
    "video_fps": 30,
    "features": {
        "video_left": {
            "type": "VISUAL",
            "shape": [3, 480, 640]
        },
        "teleop_action_left": {
            "type": "ACTION",
            "shape": [7]
        },
        "robot_state_left": {
            "type": "STATE",
            "shape": [7]
        },
        "buttons_left": {
            "type": "TEXT",
            "shape": []
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Recording a dataset
docs.text:
There are two ways of recording a dataset:

  • Using the buttons in the GUI
  • Using button combinations on the Quest controllers: Y + right trigger to start and stop recording.
    • Discarding a recording is done with B + right trigger

Warning

Make sure that a dataset is selected prior to recording, in order for the recording to be saved.

The recording will include a couple seconds before the start of a recording, and about half a second after the end of a recording if this data is available.

In order to reduce the storage space, video features should be compressed into a mp4 file, instead of raw RGB values. After a recording session, you can run the following command to compress any newly recorded demos to mp4:

cd core/scripts
python 02_process_after_record.py [relative_path_to_dataset]

docs.title: Which features are recorded?
docs.text:
There are some features which are always recorded:

  • "teleop_action_left": {"type": "ACTION", "shape": [7]}, This is the teleop_action as received from the teleoperation app, with x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, gripper commands from the left controller
  • "teleop_action_right": {"type": "ACTION", "shape": [7]}, This is the teleop_action as received from the teleoperation app, with x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, gripper commands from the right controller
  • "buttons_left": {"type": "TEXT", "shape": []}, The json string for all buttons of the left teleop controller
  • "buttons_right": {"type": "TEXT", "shape": []}, The json string for all buttons of the right teleop controller

Then, there are the robot states which are recorded for each robot that is sending out state on the robot state channel (more information here). The shape should match the size of the robot state that you are sending out.

  • "robot_state_{ROBOT_ID}": {"type": "STATE", "shape": [...]},

Each incoming video stream is recorded under with as key the video stream ID

Finally, each datachannel is recorded under the label of the datachannel. The data will be attempted to be parsed to a np.ndarray.

docs.title: Recording failure cases
docs.text:
A couple failure cases exist and will be printed to the terminal in case they are found. Note that no data is recorded in the case of a failure:

  1. Not all features as established in dataset_config.json are received. Make sure that all features you want to record are actually recorded as described here. Also make sure there are no typos, and that the robot is actually sending out the data.

  2. The feature type established in dataset_config.json differs from the received type

  3. The shape if the received data does not correspond to the shape established in dataset_config.json

docs.title: Workspace Structure
docs.text:
The workspace expects the following folders:

ws/
├── datasets/
├── policies/
└── skills/

We use a convention to also include a datasets_processed for storing pre-processed datasets, but this is not required, since the processed datasets can always be recovered from the raw datasets and do not need to be stored long-term.

You will be prompted to set your workspace folder upon the first time you start the app. Furthermore, you can always configure your workspace in the settings (make sure to restart the app afterwards):

While datasets might be straightforward, it is good to understand the difference between a skill and a policy. A skill can be defined as the semantic definition of what you want the robot to do: for instance to pour coffee or to clean the sink. A policy however, is a specific implementation of a skill or of multiple skills: for instance, a model that has been trained on pouring coffee demos with a head camera as input, versus a model that has been trained on pouring coffee demos with an end-effector camera as input. A policy could also be trained on demos from various tasks, so that it can be an implementation for various different skills.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text: This is the folder where all raw datasets are stored. Each dataset will get their own folder. For more information about datasets, see the dataset documentation.

docs.title: Policies
docs.text: This is the folder where model checkpoints will be stored. For more information about training policies, see the training documentation.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text: This is the folder where skill config files are stored. For more information about skills, see the skills documentation.
